hook.line: Vibe coding rabbit holes part eight: check out what I built with Lovable.
hook.visual: Top half: the dark 'Optimize for Search & AI' tool he built on a blue backdrop; bottom half: him in a hoodie, yellow 'Vibecoding Rabbit Hole Part 8' then 'Save for later' label.

beats.what: Series label 'Part 8' over a split screen: his finished tool on top, his face below.
Yellow 'Save for later' label replaces the title as he says what he built.
Punch to an infographic comparing traditional SEO with GEO as he defines GEO.
Says paid tools cost hundreds a month, so he built one; label 'So I built one with Lovable'.
Punch-in; mid-video ask to comment 'GEO' for the prompt and to follow.
Live demo: pastes his company website into the tool and hits analyze.
Results screen with SEO and GEO scores; label 'Industry benchmarks'.
Scrolls detailed recommendations; label 'Detailed recommendations to improve'.
Cut to the Lovable editor showing the Firecrawl integration enabled.
Cut; repeats the 'comment GEO' and follow ask, then a black end frame.

why_it_works: The finished tool is on screen from frame one, so the viewer sees the result before hearing how it was made.
'Part 8' of a series plus a 'Save for later' label prompt saves and binge-watching of earlier parts.
A free DIY version of a tool that 'costs hundreds a month' gives a clear money reason to keep watching.
The comment-keyword ask comes twice, once before the demo payoff and once at the end.
weaknesses: Fast talking (4.5 words/s) over dense UI; the median frame has 43 words on screen, too small to read on a phone.
Only 2 cuts in 79 s; the 66 s first shot relies on screen scrolling for change.
Quiet audio (-24.4 LUFS) and no music bed.
for_robert: Put the finished result on the top half from the first frame and ask for the comment keyword once before the payoff; have Fred point at one readable number instead of scrolling dense UI.
